First listed 2026-06-12 · episode or wrap

Google Raises $85 Billion and the Market Finally Wakes Up | The Weekly Wrap

The wrap develops Eisman's thesis that AI is shifting funding risk onto public shareholders through equity issuance and higher capital intensity. He contrasts strong Oracle demand with its cash burden and questions model moats and future IPO absorption. He also warns about a 4.5% Treasury threshold, concentrated earnings growth, addiction-related litigation and private-market illiquidity. Primary records support the large financing packages, inflation figures and filed lawsuit while leaving causal market explanations and most forward returns unsettled.

How he reasons here

  • Compare cash demands with reported earnings and backlog.
  • Separate headline aggregate growth from sector concentration.
  • Assess illiquidity and benchmark crowding as distinct risks.
  • Treat equity issuance and long payoff horizons as investor burdens.
